Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right apical cavitary lesion containing a mobile intracavitary mass surrounded by an air crescent sign, which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is consistent with patients who have pre-existing apical lung cavities, such as those with bullous disease associated with Marfan syndrome.
